etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 何(ど)方(ち) (dochi, “where, which way”), with addition of 促(そく)音(おん) (sokuon).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/idure/ → /idore/ → /dore/
Shift from いずれ (izure).
Compare development of 何処 (izuko → doko, “where”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From にこり (nikori, “with a bright smile”). The element にこ (niko) is onomatopoeic for smiling, and also seen in にこにこ (nikoniko, “with a grin, smile”) and にこやか (nikoyaka, “smiling”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Unknown. There are several origin theories, including:
* From ハヅレ (hazure, “other; extraordinary”)
* Of obsolete forms ハ, meaning “open; unfold”, and ズ, meaning “unlimited; without end”
* Abbreviation of 手(て)はず (tehazu, “arrangement; plan”)
* Abbreviation of obsolete ハスヱ (hasue, “tip; end”)
* From 羽(は) (ha, “feather”) and 頭(ず) (zu, “tip; head”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from Portuguese pinta (“a point, a mark”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English pin.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English ping.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Syllabic abbreviation of ラジオカセット (rajio kasetto), from English radio cassette recorder.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese compound 中心 (MC trjuwng sim, literally “heart in the middle”). Compare modern Hakka reading chûng-sîm.
From 中 (chū, “center”) + 心 (shin, “core”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 優 (MC 'juw).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the verb 勝(まさ)る (masaru, “to be superior to, to excel, to surpass, to rival”). Related to 優(まさ)しげ (masashige).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 優(すぐ)る (suguru), the Classical Japanese form of the verb 優(すぐ)れる (sugureru, “to be good at (a thing), to be superior to (a person)”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From older 助(たす)く (tasuku), a compound of 手(た) (ta-, “hand”) + 助(す)く (suku, “to help”). First appears in the late 900s.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru. For the Old / Classical form, see the 助く entry.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 助く (suku), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 可愛(かわい)い (kawaii) + らしい (-rashii).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 小(こ) (ko-, “little”) + 指(ゆび) (yubi, “finger or toe; digit”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 小(しょう) (shō, “small, little”) + 数(すう) (sū, “number”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 心 (shin, “heart”) + 理 (ri, “basic principle”).
;"psychology"

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 怒(いか)る (ikaru, “to get angry”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 怒(おこ)る (okoru, “to get angry”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/idaku/ → /daku/
Shift from idaku.
Compare the shift of 茨(いばら) (ibara, “bramble, briar”) → 薔薇(ばら) (bara, “rose”), or Classical いでる (ideru) and いだす (idasu) to modern 出(で)る (deru, “to come out, to appear”) and 出(だ)す (dasu, “to take out, to put out”).
First cited to the Utsubo Monogatari of roughly 999 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/udaku/ → /idaku/
Shift from earlier udaku.
This reading is possibly cited to a work from roughly 850 CE. However, that citation is phonologically ambiguous, and may represent the reading udaku instead. The first unambiguous citation for the idaku reading is in the Tosa Nikki of roughly 935 CE.
While there are numerous examples of mu shifting to u in various words, the mu- → u- → i- shift is unusual, and is shared only by mubara → ubara → ibara (茨, “bramble, briar”).
Found more commonly in 和(わ)文(ぶん) (wabun, “texts written primarily in native Japanese vocabulary”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨mudaku⟩ → /mudaku/ → /udaku/
Shift from Old Japanese 抱(むだ)く (mudaku), in turn possibly a compound of 身(む) (mu, “body”, combining reading) + 綰(た)く (taku, “to gather in the hands; to work or operate something with the hands”).
First cited to a text from roughly 810 CE.
This reading is encountered more in the context of 漢(かん)文(ぶん)訓(くん)読(どく) (kanbun kundoku, “the Japanese reading of texts written primarily in a variety of Classical Chinese”), and it fell out of use in roughly the Kamakura period.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Possibly a shift from 担(かた)ぐ (katagu) below. Alternatively, a doublet of 被ぐ (katsugu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Verbalization of 肩(かた) (kata, “shoulder”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 文字 (MC mjun dziH, literally “writing + character”). Compare modern Cantonese reading man⁴ zi⁶.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/mond͡ʑi/ → /mod͡ʑi/
Sound shift from monji above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 映画(えいが) (eiga, “movie”) + 館(かん) (-kan, “building”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Ultimately from Middle Chinese 正面 (MC tsyeng|tsyengH mjienH).
First attested in the early 1200s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Alternative spelling of 真面 (matomo), swapping out the broadly synonymous kanji 真 for 正.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 水(すい) (sui, “water”) + 面(めん) (men, “surface”), a compound of two Sino-Xenic elements. Compare modern Mandarin 水面 (shuǐmiàn).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 水(み) (mi, “water”) + な (na, “of”) + 面(も) (mo, “surface”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 水(み) (mi, “water”) + の (no, “of”) + 面(も) (mo, “surface”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Alteration of 交(か)わし (kawashi, “an exchange”), from 交(か)わす (kawasu, “to exchange”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 留(る)守(す) (rusu, “absence”) + 番(ばん) (ban, “watch”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Sinitic, composed of 直 (choku, “direct, straight”) + 前 (zen, “front, forward; before”). Date of borrowing unknown.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kipu/ → /kiɸu/ → */kiwu/ → /kiu/ → /kyuː/.
From Middle Chinese 級 (MC kip).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the Qin dynasty practice of rewarding combatants in war with a promotion for each enemy head that they severed. Compare Chinese 首級 /首级 (shǒují).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Sinitic 記入 /记入 (jìrù).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 誤(あやま)る (ayamaru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From kei (警, guard against) + bi (備, preparations).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: See止(や)める (yameru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Noun derived from the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem form”) of verb 鏈る (kusaru, “to be linked together, to link together”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Noun derived from the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem form”) of verb 鎖す (tozasu, “to shut and lock a door or gate”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Noun derived from the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem form”) of verb 連る (tsugaru, “to continue, to lead onto the next, to be connected; to connect or link together”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 鎻 or 鎖 (MC swaX). Compare modern Mandarin 鎖 /锁 (suǒ, “lock, padlock; shackles, chains”).
Only used in compounds in modern Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Alteration from sau, itself an alternative reading of sa above, possibly influenced by an early variety of Mandarin reading suǒ or Cantonese reading so². The shift from sau to jau (modern jō) was probably the influence of the reading of synonymous character 錠 (jō).
/sa/ → /sau/ → /d͡ʑau/ → /d͡ʑoː/

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 響(ひび)く (hibiku, “to echo”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
高(たか) (taka, root of 高(たか)い (takai, “high, tall”)) + める (-meru, “-ify, -en”), developed from Classical Japanese 高(たか)む (takamu).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
